subject: Follow-up: scope for deletion requests, backup timelines, and evidence needs
messages:
From: Alice Moore <alice.moore@finapex.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: K. Barnes <procurement@finapex.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — deletion scope & backups

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo this morning — it answered a lot of our questions about latency and model routing. Before we move into procurement we need to confirm a few specifics around Delete / RTBF:

- When a user-level Delete request is issued via the API, what stores are immediately purged vs. what remains until backup rotation? We have strict requirements that PII not be recoverable after 30 days.
- Do embeddings generated for a user get removed as part of the same delete flow?
- What logging/evidence can you provide to demonstrate completion (audit record, deletion IDs, timestamped log export)?
- For Dedicated/private customers: are there options to accelerate removal from backups or is the weekly snapshot retention immutable?

Ideally we need a short one-page statement we can attach to our security review and an initial SLA for deletion timelines (for procurement). Can you also call out any situations that would prevent deletion (legal hold, export requests)?

Appreciate a short recap and next steps.

Best,
Alice Moore
Head of Security & Compliance
FinApex

Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — deletion scope & backups

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (privacy/ops) to confirm specifics and draft the short statement for your security review. Quick answers from my side:

- Active stores: user records and associated artifacts (raw inputs, generated outputs) are removed from the active dataset and serving indices within 24 hours of a successful Delete API call.
- Embeddings: embeddings tied to a user ID are removed as part of the same delete flow. We will include the exact API field names in the statement.
- Evidence: we can provide an audit export showing the deletion event ID, timestamp, operator (system/service), and the API request ID.
- Backups: by default weekly snapshots are retained according to the configured retention window (standard: 30 days). For Dedicated customers we can discuss an expedited process but it depends on snapshot immutability and any existing legal holds.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm the technical purge window and exception cases.
2) Marissa to draft the one-page deletion statement + list of artifacts we can provide.
3) I’ll coordinate a 30-minute technical call early next week with your security team to walk through evidence and SLA wording.

Proposed time slots: Wed 5/5 10–11am PT or Thu 5/6 9–10am PT. Pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — deletion scope & backups

Thanks Soojin — adding the technical details Alice requested. I want to be explicit so procurement has a clear expectation.

Technical delete flow (high level):
- Step 1: API request received; request validated and enqueued.
- Step 2 (T+0 to T+24): Active object store and serving indices (including embeddings index) are removed. Any in-memory KV caches and model-level prefix caches are invalidated immediately.
- Step 3 (T+24 to T+72): Asynchronous background job ensures downstream materialized views and derived indices are scrubbed.
- Backups/Snapshots: Weekly snapshots are immutable by default for integrity. Standard retention window is 30 days.

Exceptions / acceleration options:
- Dedicated deployments: we can run a targeted snapshot retention override where we restore the snapshot, prune records, and re-snapshot — this is operationally invasive and requires a change freeze window and a signed authorization from the customer (legal/ops). Typical lead time: 3–10 business days depending on region and snapshot size.
- Legal hold / active litigation: deletion will be paused until the hold is lifted; we can provide the acknowledgement and the legal hold ID in evidence exports.

Evidence artifacts we can provide (examples):
- Deletion event export (CSV) with deletion_event_id, user_id, timestamp, api_request_id
- Audit log excerpt showing job progression and status codes (JSON lines)
- Snapshot manifest showing affected snapshot IDs and retention timestamps (for audit)

I’ve attached a short diagram and the runbook extract for your security team to review (attachment stubs). If FinApex wants an accelerated path on Dedicated we should capture that in procurement as an addendum to the SLA (one-time operational fee may apply).

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: deletion_flow_diagram.pdf (diagram), redwood-deletion-runbook-extract.txt (runbook excerpt)

Hi Alice — quick compliance note and content for the one-page statement.

Items we will include in the statement:
- Declarative scope: what "Delete" covers (user profile, inputs, outputs, embeddings, derived indices) and the default timelines for active store purge.
- Backup commitments: standard retention policy and the Dedicated accelerated-removal process with required approvals and estimated lead times.
- Audit evidence types: deletion_event exports, audit_log slices, snapshot manifests, and optional notarized timestamp from our KMS when keys are rotated.
- Limitations: legal holds, court orders, and third-party archival exports (if FinApex pushes logs to an external SIEM) are outside Redwood's control.

I’ll draft the one-pager and attach the sample deletion_event CSV schema and an example audit slice (redacted). Expect a first draft by EOD Wed (5/5). I’ve uploaded the sample artifacts to the link below for your team to preview: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/privacy/finapex-rtbf-evidence

If you need the statement to be signed/dated for procurement, let me know and we’ll generate a formal evidence packet that includes a dated cover letter and the log extracts.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
